title: Migrated ledger validation against the prior accounting system
prompt: Validate a newly migrated ledger against the prior accounting system using trial balance, financial statements, open AR/AP and bank balances.

setup.q: How do the prior system's accounts map to Dime's chart of accounts (a mapping table or the rule used)?
What is the cutover date (the as-of date the migrated balances represent)?
What difference per account is accepted as rounding (0 means penny-exact)?

inputs.name: Prior system trial balance as of the cutover date
Prior system balance sheet and profit and loss as of the cutover date
Prior system open AR and AP agings as of the cutover date
Prior system bank balances or bank reconciliations as of the cutover date

steps: run column_map over the legacy trial balance and agings (headers never positions) and save the mapping to data/legacy-tb-columns.json
apply the account mapping; list legacy accounts with no Dime account and Dime accounts with no legacy source
pull Dime's trial balance as of the cutover date, the balance sheet and profit and loss, the AR and AP agings and the bank account balances
compare account by account, customer by customer, vendor by vendor and bank account by bank account; a difference above the tolerance is an exception with both figures
tie: legacy total debits and credits equal Dime's, and each subledger total equals its control account

done.text: The Dime trial balance total on the Tie-out equals Dime's own trial balance as of the cutover date
The legacy trial balance and aging columns were mapped by header with no ambiguous or missing required column
Every exception row cites the legacy account or record and the Dime account or record id
migration-validation.xlsx opens with Exceptions first (count and total on the first rows), a Tie-out block whose Difference is 0.00, and no internal plumbing words
Every difference above the tolerance is listed per account with the legacy and Dime figures; unmapped accounts on either side are their own exceptions and nothing is netted across accounts
